name: Odd One Out
mechanic: Find the one item differing from an identical majority by shape, color or orientation.
interaction: Tap the single anomalous item before time expires.
object: A rotated minority form against a repeated majority.
distinction: Form and orientation deviance, rather than Visual Search’s simple filled-tile singleton.
concept: One sideways triangle stands apart from an otherwise identical upright group.

name: Signal Watch
mechanic: Tap GO for each streamed digit except the stop digit, which requires withholding.
interaction: Tap or deliberately do nothing on each number.
object: A numeral stream interrupted by a stop sign.
distinction: Simple digit-based inhibition, not Cue Keeper’s changing memorized set of symbols.
concept: A stream of digits meets a central stop-digit boundary and a withheld response.

name: Symbol Tracker
mechanic: Remember highlighted symbol identities, then find them after a discrete board scramble adds distractors.
interaction: Tap the previously tracked identities in their new cells.
object: An identifiable star relocated between two boards.
distinction: Track identity through a scramble, rather than recall original positions or follow continuous motion.
concept: The same ringed star changes position between two boards while decoys surround it.

name: Target Count
mechanic: Count occurrences of a target glyph in a briefly shown mixed field, then choose the total.
interaction: Select the numerical count, not the position of a target.
object: A countable set of repeated stars and one total chip.
distinction: Multiple target occurrences and a quantity response, rather than a singleton search.
concept: Three obvious target stars among subdued distractors lead to a numerical total.

name: Visual Search
mechanic: Find the one colored tile among identical surface tiles before the round expires.
interaction: Tap the visually distinct filled tile.
object: A search lens framing one filled tile.
distinction: A simple color-filled singleton; Odd One Out instead compares repeated forms and orientation.
concept: A large magnifying lens isolates the single filled tile in a pale tile field.

name: Card Sort
mechanic: Match a target by color or shape across rule blocks, including hidden-rule discovery stretches.
interaction: Pick one of four cards under the active sorting rule and adapt after notice of a switch.
object: A target card above a fan of four candidates, with one shape match lifted.
distinction: Physical card sorting with two attributes and rule-switch notice; there are no number attributes.
concept: An oversized triangle card sorts to a lifted triangle in a four-card fan with color lures.

name: Color Stroop
mechanic: Resolve conflicting word meaning and ink color according to the current ink-or-word rule.
interaction: Read the active rule, then select the appropriate color answer.
object: The native word RED printed in blue ink, with a blue answer selected.
distinction: Semantic word-versus-ink conflict, not card attributes or a plain color swatch match.
concept: A large color word conflicts with its ink; a curved arrow selects the ink-color answer.

name: Cue Shift
mechanic: An explicit trial cue selects color, shape or number as the target-matching rule.
interaction: Read each cue and select the candidate matching only the named attribute.
object: Three attribute selectors above two cards whose shape matches but color and number disagree.
distinction: The explicit attribute selector is the subject; the rule may repeat but is cued each trial.
concept: A shape cue selects matching triangles while native numbers and colors disagree.

name: Rule Flip
mechanic: Maintain a color, shape or number rule across a run of trials, then adapt to block flips and uncued stretches.
interaction: Match the target to one candidate, retaining or inferring the rule until it changes.
object: A hinged physical rule tile turns from shape to number.
distinction: A sustained rule flips at a block boundary; unlike Cue Shift, rule persistence and inference matter.
concept: A large raised shape face pivots over the number-rule face with a single flip arrow.

name: Task Switch
mechanic: Apply a cued parity, low/high magnitude or color classification to one number-bearing token.
interaction: Read the micro-task cue and select the correct verbal classification.
object: One number token branches to ODD and HIGH task answers.
distinction: Classify a single token under different tasks, rather than matching target and candidate cards.
concept: A large seven has two task branches showing its parity and magnitude classifications.

name: Context Fit
mechanic: Select the one word best completing a sentence’s meaning.
interaction: Read the sentence and tap the fitting word option.
object: Sentence sheet with a word-shaped blank and a semantically fitting word card.
distinction: Fills a contextual sentence gap; Sentence Builder instead orders all word chips.
concept: A sentence sheet says Birds build their ? while a nests word card approaches the blank.

name: Sentence Builder
mechanic: Reconstruct a scrambled sentence in a valid grammatical word order.
interaction: Tap full-word chips in sequence under a category hint and round timer.
object: Separate whole-word chips on a sentence assembly rail.
distinction: Orders words, whereas Word Scramble recognizes an unscrambled single word from letters.
concept: Multiple shuffled whole-word chips fly, Birds, can reorder into the complete Birds can fly sentence rail.

name: Word Chain
mechanic: Complete missing lexical links where the next word begins with the previous word’s last letter.
interaction: Select successive missing word options in a chain.
object: Descending word cards joined by directional links and matching endpoint-letter accents.
distinction: Uses spelling endpoints rather than semantic synonyms or sentence grammar.
concept: Follow CAT → TREE → EAGLE, joining each final letter to the next initial letter.

name: Word Match
mechanic: Recognize the best synonym of a prompt word among four options.
interaction: Tap the word with the same meaning before the deadline.
object: Two matching-meaning speech bubbles.
distinction: Semantic equivalence rather than identical spelling, anagram formation, or terminal-letter chains.
concept: Two facing speech bubbles pair happy and glad across an equivalence sign.

name: Word Scramble
mechanic: Recognize the word represented by a letter scramble using a category hint.
interaction: Select an unscrambled word option and submit; rounds are untimed.
object: Scattered individual letters above one resolved word card.
distinction: Letters within one word, not whole-word sentence ordering; the player selects rather than drags letters.
concept: Loose V R R E I letter pieces resolve to one intact RIVER word-choice card.

name: Code Cracker
mechanic: Deduce a hidden color code from exact-position and color-only feedback after guesses.
interaction: Build a color guess and submit, then use feedback to refine the next guess.
object: Code pegboard with a concealed row, a guess row, and a separate feedback cluster.
distinction: Logical feedback-driven code deduction rather than memorizing or directly matching colors.
concept: A concealed four-peg code sits above a colored guess and filled versus outline feedback pegs.

name: Deduction Table
mechanic: Use equality, exclusion and inequality clues to infer one uniquely determined entity attribute.
interaction: Read the table and clues, then choose the asked value.
object: A row-labeled dossier table with pictorial attribute headers and a clue slip.
distinction: Entity attributes and external clues; Rule Grid instead applies one Latin row/column rule.
concept: A labeled entity-by-attribute table carries one asked cell and an attached A-not-triangle clue slip.

name: Next in Sequence
mechanic: Infer a numerical pattern and choose its next term.
interaction: Inspect the visible terms and tap the correct continuation.
object: Ordered number tokens ending in a conspicuous unknown.
distinction: Infers an unseen rule rather than recalling shown order or ranking magnitudes.
concept: A numeric progression 2, 4, 8, ? follows repeated curved continuation arrows.

name: Order Path
mechanic: Solve a uniquely ordered precedence puzzle from before/after constraints.
interaction: Tap each lettered item in the only valid order.
object: Lettered precedence graph and ordered placement slots.
distinction: Topological order of letters, not spatial navigation or numerical continuation.
concept: Directed A → B → C precedence nodes feed an ordered A, B, ? slot rail.

name: Rule Grid
mechanic: Deduce an asked Latin-square cell; each row and column contains every symbol once, with chained unknowns on harder levels.
interaction: Inspect the grid and tap the only symbol fitting the asked cell.
object: Latin numeral board with one targeted blank and intersecting constraint bands.
distinction: Constraint-based symbol deduction, not memory pattern recall or entity-attribute clues.
concept: A valid 3×3 Latin grid highlights the row and column that force its central missing 3.

name: Equation Builder
mechanic: Construct an expression using every given number to reach a target, respecting precedence and optional grouping.
interaction: Tap supplied number and operator pieces, then submit the constructed equation.
object: Number pieces on an expression rail beneath a target medallion.
distinction: Builds the expression itself; Fast Math supplies the expression and Missing Operator omits only an operator.
concept: Assemble 3 + 4 + 5 on a construction rail to reach the separate target 12.

name: Fast Math
mechanic: Solve validated exact arithmetic against a round budget.
interaction: Type the numeric answer on a number pad and submit.
object: Calculator display and keypad with a subordinate timing dial.
distinction: Produces the numerical answer to a supplied expression rather than selecting a symbol or arranging values.
concept: A calculator face presents 7 + 5 = ? above number-entry keys, accompanied by a small stopwatch.

name: Missing Operator
mechanic: Find the unique operator that makes a fixed equation true.
interaction: Tap one of the four operator choices.
object: An operator-shaped gap with an incoming multiplication tile.
distinction: Only the operator is unknown; all operands and the result are supplied.
concept: Choose the multiplication tile that fills the operator gap in 8 × 2 = 16.

name: Number Line
mechanic: Estimate a target number’s continuous position between labeled endpoints.
interaction: Tap or adjust a draft position, then submit the estimate.
object: Horizontal calibrated ruler and movable position marker.
distinction: Continuous spatial interpolation rather than discrete ranking of tiles.
concept: Place a movable marker for 40 on a calibrated 0–100 ruler.

name: Value Order
mechanic: Rank a shuffled set of distinct numeric values, including expression-disguised values.
interaction: Tap every tile from smallest value to largest; a wrong tap ends the round.
object: A magnitude staircase with an expression-valued middle block.
distinction: Expression evaluation plus relative magnitude, unlike Speed’s ordinary number sweep.
concept: Ascending magnitude steps read 3, 2 × 4, and 12 under a rising ordering arrow.

name: Memory
mechanic: Watch a sequence of distinct positions on a grid, then reproduce their original order.
interaction: Tap the previously illuminated cells in order.
object: Scattered sequential flashes on a tile board.
distinction: Arbitrary positional jumps and no repeats, rather than an adjacent path or repeat-capable Simon pads.
concept: Scattered flashing positions carry an ordered 1–2–3 recall sequence.

name: Grid Recall
mechanic: Study a simultaneous set of lit cells and rebuild the same set after it hides.
interaction: Select the remembered positions, with no required selection order.
object: One whole highlighted spatial pattern.
distinction: Recall the set of positions, not an ordered flashing sequence.
concept: A whole illuminated cell pattern is echoed as an empty remembered arrangement.

name: Pair Recall
mechanic: Learn shape-to-letter associations, then recall the partner of a cued shape; pairings change between rounds.
interaction: Tap the remembered partner letter.
object: A shape and its distinct letter partner.
distinction: Association recall, not a facedown card-pair search.
concept: A shape card is linked to its letter partner, with a recall loop beneath.

name: Pattern Tap Back
mechanic: Watch a nonrepeating path of cells flash, with each step next to the previous cell, then repeat it.
interaction: Tap the adjacent route in the original order.
object: A continuous stepping-stone path.
distinction: Neighbor-to-neighbor path recall, unlike the arbitrary jumps of Memory.
concept: A connected trail of neighboring tactile tiles ends at a tap ripple.

name: Cue Keeper
mechanic: Hold a changing memorized symbol watchlist and respond SIGNAL when an active symbol appears in a stream.
interaction: Tap GO for other symbols and SIGNAL for the memorized intentions.
object: A pinned memory pocket, arriving star and distinct SIGNAL control.
distinction: Remember changing prospective intentions; no continuously displayed reminder and no stop-digit withholding.
concept: A pinned symbol watchlist is retained while an arriving matching star calls for the explicit SIGNAL response.

name: Running Order
mechanic: Watch a symbol stream, discard its older items, and recall only the trailing few in order.
interaction: Tap the last symbols in their original order after the stream ends.
object: A sliding trailing-memory window and empty response slots.
distinction: Only the temporal tail matters; these are symbols, not numbers to sort.
concept: Faded earlier symbols leave a crisp last-three window, then a recall arrow returns to three empty slots.

name: Sequence Memory
mechanic: Repeat an increasingly long Simon-style sequence, including legal nonadjacent repeated pads, in a score attack.
interaction: Tap the colored pads in the observed sequence.
object: A single four-color tactile pad console.
distinction: Repeat-capable colored-pad sequences; unlike Memory, a pad can recur in one sequence.
concept: Four colored tactile Simon pads form one console, with one pad actively pulsing.

name: Coordinate Turn
mechanic: Follow relative turn and movement commands on a free plane to determine heading or position.
interaction: Track orientation and choose a final direction or coordinate.
object: A compass needle pivoting from north to east.
distinction: Orientation around a pivot, rather than a bounded board route or object rotation.
concept: A large compass with a ghost north needle, solid east needle and clockwise turn arc.

name: Fold Match
mechanic: Study a marked grid, then choose its paper-folded OR-merged result.
interaction: Memorize the sheet and fold cue, then tap the correct folded pattern.
object: One paper sheet with a raised flap, crease and half-width kept base.
distinction: Paper folding merges marks and shrinks the sheet; this is not reflection on an unchanged board.
concept: One raised paper flap casts a trapezoid shadow; exact mirrored marks merge onto the kept half.

name: Grid Navigator
mechanic: Follow forward, back and relative turn commands inside a bounded square grid.
interaction: Trace the marker mentally, then choose the small board marking its final cell.
object: A contiguous elbow route from hollow start to directional destination.
distinction: The visible start-to-end route dominates a bounded board; no disconnected memory cells.
concept: A five-by-five navigation board carries one bold continuous two-turn route.

name: Mental Rotation
mechanic: Judge whether a colored connected 2D block shape is a rotated copy or a different arrangement.
interaction: Compare target and candidate, then choose Same or Different.
object: An asymmetric green, cyan and gold F pentomino and its true clockwise quarter-turn.
distinction: Free connected block silhouettes with attached colors, not filled-cell grid transformations.
concept: Two identical asymmetric polyominoes preserve three distinct block colors through an exact clockwise quarter-turn.

name: Transform Match
mechanic: Memorize a briefly shown pattern, then infer and select the correct rotated or mirrored result.
interaction: Recall the hidden source pattern and tap its correct transformed candidate.
object: Equal-size pattern panels on opposite sides of a mirror axis.
distinction: Fixed board size and preserved cell count separate reflection from shrinking OR-folds.
concept: Two sparse asymmetric patterns reflect exactly across a visible vertical mirror axis.

name: Color Match
mechanic: Choose the response matching the swatch color while ignoring the ink color of the accompanying word.
interaction: Tap the button with the swatch’s hue as quickly as possible.
object: A large color swatch above three color response chips.
distinction: Match a visible swatch; do not solve Color Stroop’s changing word-versus-ink task.
concept: A large physical blue swatch connects directly to its matching blue response chip.

name: Order Sweep
mechanic: Scan numbers all visible at once and clear them from smallest to largest before the timer drains.
interaction: Tap the number tokens in ascending order.
object: A spatial sweep through shuffled numeral discs.
distinction: Simultaneous plain integers, rather than Running Order’s temporal symbols or Value Order’s expressions.
concept: A sweeping stroke links scattered number tokens from 2 to 5 to 9.

name: Quick Compare
mechanic: Judge equality, greater magnitude or the larger sum for two shown values under time pressure.
interaction: Choose the correct comparison answer before the response window closes.
object: Two facing numeric stimulus cards.
distinction: One paired numeric decision, rather than constructing arithmetic or sweeping an entire number field.
concept: Two large numerical cards face one another across a bold comparison sign.

name: Reaction Time
mechanic: Wait for the signal; respond quickly to green and withhold on no-go trials.
interaction: Tap the stationary signal after it appears.
object: Raised green signal button.
distinction: One stationary signal, rather than the changing positions of Tap Rush.
concept: One stationary green signal button: wait, then react.

name: Tap Rush
mechanic: Hit one appearing circular target at a time before its window closes as targets change field position.
interaction: Tap the target’s current position; misses and empty-field taps break the streak.
object: A single pop-up target and fading previous positions.
distinction: Rapid spatial aiming, unlike Reaction Time’s one stationary signal button.
concept: One active circular target bursts with a tap ripple while prior positions fade across open space.
